children: Long-dated Treasury yields rise as a hostilities flare-up in Hormuz pushes oil up 3% and rekindles inflation fears. The 10-year adds 0.036 percentage point today (0.014 p.p. this month) to 4.757%, its highest settle since January 2025. The increase belies Treasury Secretary Bessent's efforts to cool down long-term yields. Tomorrow, job openings in July JOLTS report are likely to remain at 7.4 million, according to a WSJ consensus. August payrolls, on Friday, are forecast to add 50,000, after losing 23,000 in July. The two-year yield in unchanged at 4.348%, but still ends the month up 0.059 p.p. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)
